mainTopic: Whether תקנת אושא can be proven, who keeps the money from selling the טובת הנאה of a כתובה, and why a married woman who injures someone cannot pay.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about witnesses who falsely said a married woman already got her כתובה. They pay only its טובת הנאה, meaning what a buyer would pay for it, knowing the husband inherits her if she dies first. The גמרא tries to use this ruling to prove תקנת אושא, but אביי pushes the proof away by pointing to נכסי צאן ברזל. אביי then says the money from selling the טובת הנאה belongs to the wife. רב שלמן weakens his proof, and רבא rules that the money is hers and the husband does not even eat its profits. Next, רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע bring a new proof for תקנת אושא from the משנה about a wife who injures someone. The גמרא rejects that proof: the משנה must be about a woman with no נכסי מלוג. The גמרא then asks why she cannot sell her כתובה's טובת הנאה to pay, and tries several answers: רבי מאיר, 'just words', and שמואל's rule about cancelling a debt. It ends on the idea that she would surely forgive her husband, and starts a new suggestion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ruling: false witnesses pay only the market value of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that when the witnesses are found to be עדים זוממין while the woman is still married, they do not pay her full כתובה. They pay only its טובת הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she is actually still married to him and serving him, and the witnesses were found to be זוממין. The court does not say they pay her whole כתובה, only the טובת הנאה of her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא. It says that lying witnesses who tried to wipe out a married woman's כתובה pay only its 'market value' (טובת הנאה), not the full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She has not lost the full כתובה right now, because she was never going to collect it while still married. What she lost is the right she holds today, a right that may or may not ever be paid. So the witnesses pay what that uncertain right is worth.

keyTerms.meaning: Under him, meaning still married to him
Plotting witnesses, proven false because they were elsewhere at the time
The money a wife collects if she is widowed or divorced
The small market value of an uncertain right

phrases.english: and she is under him and serves him;
phrases.notes: Meaning the couple is really still married, so the witnesses' story was false.

phrases.english: and they were found to be plotting witnesses;
we do not say they pay her entire כתובה,
rather the financial advantage of her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין אוֹמְרִים יְשַׁלְּמוּ כׇּל כְּתוּבָּתָהּ, אֶלָּא טוֹבַת הֲנָאַת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section, quoted as proof for תקנת אושא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין who tried to cancel a married woman's כתובה pay only its טובת הנאה, not its full value.

steps.title: How the market value of a כתובה is calculated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines טובת הנאה: how much a buyer would pay for her כתובה, knowing he collects if she is widowed or divorced, but gets nothing if she dies first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the טובת הנאה of her כתובה? We estimate how much a person would pay for this woman's כתובה. If she is widowed or divorced, he collects. But if she dies, her husband inherits her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how to put a price on the כתובה. It is a gamble: the buyer wins if she outlives the marriage and loses if she dies first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the last line: if she dies, her husband inherits her, so the buyer gets nothing. That risk is what makes the price low. The גמרא will now use this exact detail as the proof.

phrases.english: What is the financial advantage of her כתובה?
We estimate how much a person would want to give
for the כתובה of this woman –
since if she is widowed or divorced,
but if she dies – her husband inherits her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term טובת הנאה from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טובת הנאה is the price a buyer would pay, knowing that if she dies first her husband inherits and the buyer collects nothing.

steps.title: Proof that תקנת אושא exists
steps.stepSummary: Without תקנת אושא, she could sell her כתובה completely and the husband could not take it back. Since the ברייתא says he does inherit, תקנת אושא must exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think there is no תקנת אושא, why would her husband inherit her? She could sell her כתובה completely!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main point of the quote. The גמרא uses the line 'her husband inherits her' to prove that תקנת אושא is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תקנת אושא says that if a wife sells her property and then dies, the husband can take it back from the buyer. Without that rule, a sale she made would hold up, and the buyer would keep the כתובה even after she dies. The ברייתא assumes the husband wins, so the rule must exist.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule made at אושא: the husband can take back property his wife sold, if she dies

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לֵיתַהּ לְתַקָּנַת אוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that there is no ordinance of Usha,
why would her husband inherit her?
Let her sell her כתובה completely!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לֵיתַהּ לְתַקָּנַת אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא's line that the husband inherits.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement that if she dies, her husband inherits her, so the buyer of her כתובה gets nothing.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא can be explained without תקנת אושא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Even without תקנת אושא, she could sell only her נכסי מלוג, never her נכסי צאן ברזל. So her כתובה could never be sold in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if they said she can sell her נכסי מלוג, would they say she can sell her נכסי צאן ברזל?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down the proof. The husband would inherit part of what she sold no matter what, so the ברייתא's line does not need תקנת אושא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נכסי צאן ברזל are fully in the husband's control, so she can never sell them, with or without תקנת אושא. Because of that, the sale of her כתובה was never complete. The ברייתא's ruling fits even if תקנת אושא does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: Property the wife keeps owning while the husband eats its profits
'Iron sheep' property: fully under the husband's control and guaranteed by him

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying תקנת אושא doesn't exist. He is only saying this ברייתא does not prove it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If they said so regarding usufruct property,
would they say so regarding guaranteed property?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ בְּנִכְסֵי מְלוֹג, יֹאמְרוּ בְּנִכְסֵי צֹאן בַּרְזֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא, not the existence of תקנת אושא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that without תקנת אושא she could sell her whole כתובה. But נכסי צאן ברזל can never be sold by her, so the husband would inherit regardless.

steps.title: אביי: the money from selling טובת הנאה belongs to the wife
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic came up, אביי adds a new rule: the money from selling the טובת הנאה of a כתובה goes to the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since טובת הנאה has come up, let us say something about it. The טובת הנאה belongs to the wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new side topic. אביי states who keeps the money when a woman sells the market value of her כתובה: she does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether this sale money counts as the wife's own or as something the husband gets, like the profits of her property. אביי rules it is hers. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it came to our hands, meaning since we are discussing it
Let us say something about it

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Financial advantage, since it has come to our hands,
let us say something about it:
The financial advantage – belongs to the wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה, הוֹאִיל וַאֲתָא לְיָדַן, נֵימָא בַּהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the term טובת הנאה from the ברייתא and starts a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money from selling the טובת הנאה of a כתובה belongs to the wife, not the husband.

steps.title: אביי's proof: otherwise the false witnesses caused her no loss
steps.stepSummary: If the money went to the husband, the witnesses could tell her they cost her nothing. Since the ברייתא makes them pay her, the money must be hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think it belongs to the husband, the witnesses could say to her: What did we make you lose? Even if you had sold it for its טובת הנאה, your husband would have taken it from you!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his rule from the ברייתא. The witnesses pay her, so she must have lost something of her own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses only pay for real loss. If the husband took the sale money anyway, the woman never had anything to lose, and the witnesses would owe her nothing. The ברייתא's ruling that they pay shows the money is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: What loss did we cause you?

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it belongs to the husband,
let the witnesses say to her:
What loss have we caused you?

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוָה מְזַבְּנַתְּ לַהּ לְטוֹבַת הֲנָאָה,
phrases.english: If you had sold it for the financial advantage,
the husband would have taken it from you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for אביי's rule in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the money from selling טובת הנאה belongs to the wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that the עדים זוממין must pay her the טובת הנאה, which only makes sense if she suffered a real loss.

steps.title: רב שלמן: she still loses, because the household gains
steps.stepSummary: רב שלמן answers that even if the husband took the money, she would still lose, since the money would benefit the whole household she lives in. So the ברייתא does not prove אביי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שלמן said: Because there is a gain for the household.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שלמן pushes back on אביי's proof. Even if the money went to the husband, the witnesses still caused her a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed she loses nothing if the husband takes the money. רב שלמן says the money would make the home better off, and she benefits from that. So the witnesses must pay either way, and the ברייתא no longer proves who gets the money.

keyTerms.meaning: More comfort and money in the household

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about עדים זוממין and the טובת הנאה of a כתובה was brought to prove two things. It was used to prove תקנת אושא, and אביי pushed that proof away. אביי then used it to prove the wife keeps the sale money, and רב שלמן pushed that proof away with the idea of רווח ביתא.

phrases.english: Rav Shalman said:
Because there is a gain for the household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the witnesses' claim in step 6 and so weakens אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's proof from the ברייתא, not necessarily his rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed that if the husband takes the money she loses nothing. But a richer household benefits her too, so the witnesses still caused her a loss.

steps.title: The הלכה: the money is the wife's, and the husband gets no profits from it
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like אביי that the money from selling the טובת הנאה goes to the wife. He adds that the husband does not even eat the profits from it, because the רבנן gave him only 'profit', not 'profit of profit'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that the money from the טובת הנאה belongs to the wife, and the husband does not get the profits from it. Why? The רבנן gave the husband the profit of her property, but they did not give him the profit of the profit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the discussion about the טובת הנאה money with a final ruling. He also explains the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband eats the פירות (profits) of his wife's property. But the money from selling the טובת הנאה is itself already a kind of 'profit' from her כתובה. The רבנן only gave the husband one level of profit, not a second level built on top of the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha, the final practical ruling
The small present value of a doubtful future right, here the chance of collecting the כתובה
Literally 'eats the fruits': gets the profits or income of property
The profit of the profit, a second level of income

steps.whatToRemember: The טובת הנאה money belongs to the wife, and the husband does not even get the profits from it, since the רבנן never gave him 'profit of profit'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical הלכה after the proof in Step 6 was rejected in Step 7, and it sets a limit on how far the husband's rights over his wife's property go.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is:
the money from the financial advantage goes to the wife,
and the husband does not eat the profits.
What is the reason?
The profit, the Rabbis instituted for him;

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירָא דְפֵירָא לָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: the profit of the profit, the Rabbis did not institute for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for אביי's rule was rejected, רבא rules like אביי anyway and adds a further point.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The money from selling the טובת הנאה of a כתובה belongs to the wife, and the husband does not eat its profits, because 'profit of profit' was never given to him.

steps.title: A proof for תקנת אושא from the משנה about a wife who injures others
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע bring a proof from our משנה: a married woman who injures someone is exempt because she has no money. If there were no תקנת אושא, she could sell her נכסי מלוג and pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע came from the study hall, they said: We have a source for תקנת אושא in our משנה, which says: 'A slave and a woman are bad to run into. Someone who injures them must pay, but if they injure others, they are exempt.' If there were no תקנת אושא, she could sell her נכסי מלוג and pay the person she hurt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic, whether תקנת אושא exists. Two אמוראים bring a new proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under תקנת אושא, a woman's sale of her נכסי מלוג can be taken back by the husband, so she cannot really sell them. The משנה says a wife who injures someone cannot pay. That fits only if she cannot sell her נכסי מלוג, which means תקנת אושא must exist.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it (in a משנה or ברייתא)
Running into them is bad, since you lose either way
If it would enter your mind, if you thought

phrases.english: When Rav Pappa came

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, from the study hall,
they said: We have learned a source for the ordinance of Usha:
A slave and a woman, an encounter with them is bad;
phrases.notes: This is our משנה on 87a, talking about a married woman.

phrases.english: one who injures them is liable,
but if they injured others, they are exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לֵיתַהּ לְתַקָּנַת אוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: And if you think there is no ordinance of Usha,
let her sell her usufruct property and give it to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side topic of the טובת הנאה, the גמרא returns to proving תקנת אושא with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That תקנת אושא exists: a wife cannot truly sell her נכסי מלוג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 87a: a married woman who injures others is exempt, since she has no money to pay

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: she could still sell the טובת הנאה, so the case must be a woman with no property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even with תקנת אושא, she could sell her נכסי מלוג for their טובת הנאה and pay. So the משנה must be talking about a woman who has no נכסי מלוג at all, and then it proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your logic: even if there is a תקנת אושא and she cannot sell the property completely, she could still sell her נכסי מלוג for their טובת הנאה and pay him! So you must say the משנה is talking about a woman who has no such property. If so, here too, the משנה is about a woman who has none, and it proves nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It shows that the משנה has a problem even if תקנת אושא exists, so it cannot be used to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תקנת אושא only stops a full sale. A buyer could still pay a small amount now for the chance that the property becomes hers if she is widowed or divorced. Since the משנה says she cannot pay at all, it must be talking about a woman with no נכסי מלוג, and that case says nothing about תקנת אושא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning, turning the argument back on the asker
Granted that, even if we accept
Where she does not have (any property)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
granted that there is an ordinance of Usha,
and she cannot sell it completely;
let her sell her usufruct property for the financial advantage,
phrases.notes: The buyer pays a little now for the chance of owning it later, if she is widowed or divorced.

phrases.english: and give it to him!
Rather, it is where she does not have any;
so too, it is where she does not have any.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, נְהִי נָמֵי דְּאִיתַיהּ לְתַקָּנַת אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for תקנת אושא from the משנה is rejected entirely, though תקנת אושא itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same question hits even if תקנת אושא exists, so the משנה must be about a woman with no נכסי מלוג, and that case cannot prove anything.

steps.title: Why can't she sell the טובת הנאה of her כתובה to pay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה itself: even a woman with no נכסי מלוג has a כתובה. She could sell its טובת הנאה and pay the person she injured.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her sell her כתובה for its טובת הנאה and pay the person she hurt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the משנה's ruling itself. Every married woman has a כתובה, so why does the משנה say she has no way to pay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the משנה is about a woman with no נכסי מלוג. But every wife has a כתובה, and as we learned earlier, its טובת הנאה can be sold. So it seems she always has some money to pay with.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, the money a wife collects if divorced or widowed

phrases.english: But let her sell her marriage contract for the financial advantage,
and give it to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְזַבֵּין כְּתוּבְּתַהּ בְּטוֹבַת הֲנָאָה, וְתִתֵּן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 10's answer. Even a woman with no נכסי מלוג still has a כתובה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a married woman who injures others is exempt because she cannot pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every wife has a כתובה whose טובת הנאה can be sold, so she should always have some money to pay damages.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי מאיר: a wife may not be left without a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who says a man may not live with his wife even one hour without a כתובה. So she is not allowed to sell her כתובה's טובת הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי מאיר, who said: A man is forbidden to keep his wife even one hour without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she sold the טובת הנאה of her כתובה, she would be left with no כתובה of her own. According to רבי מאיר, a husband may not stay married to her even for a moment in that state. So selling her כתובה is not an option, and the משנה is right that she cannot pay.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should keep or remain with

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for תקנת אושא from the משנה fails, since the משנה is about a woman with no נכסי מלוג. The רבי מאיר answer for why she cannot sell her כתובה's טובת הנאה is only a first attempt. Step 14 knocks it down, and new reasons follow.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: It is forbidden for a man
to remain with his wife
even one hour without a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every wife could sell the טובת הנאה of her כתובה and use the money to pay damages.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, she may not be left without a כתובה even for one hour, so she cannot sell it, and she truly has no way to pay.

steps.title: What is the reason behind רבי מאיר's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר forbids living without a כתובה and answers: so the husband will not find it easy to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? So that she should not be 'light' in his eyes to send her away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי מאיר's rule, which was just used to explain the משנה. This sets up the next move, where that reason will be tested against our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is a money penalty the husband pays if he divorces. Without it, divorcing would cost him nothing, so he might divorce her easily. That is why רבי מאיר says she must always have a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Easy or unimportant in his eyes
To send her away, meaning to divorce her

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
So that she should not be light in his eyes
to send her away (to divorce her).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the רבי מאיר answer given in step 12, so it can be tested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי מאיר forbids a husband to live with his wife without a כתובה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So that divorcing her will not be easy and cost-free for him.

steps.title: That reason does not apply when she sold her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If she sold her כתובה, the husband still cannot divorce cheaply, because the buyers will collect it from him. So רבי מאיר's reason does not apply here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here he will not divorce her, because if he divorces her, the people who bought it will come and collect her כתובה from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the step 12 answer. רבי מאיר's reason does not fit a woman who sold her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling the טובת הנאה does not free the husband. If he divorces her, he still pays the full כתובה, just to the buyers instead of to her. So she is not 'without a כתובה' in the sense רבי מאיר worried about, and the answer in step 12 falls apart.

phrases.english: Here, he will not divorce her,
for if he divorces her,
those who bought will come
and collect her כתובה from him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 13 to knock down the answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's worry is a husband who can divorce for free. After a sale, he still has to pay the buyers, so the worry does not exist.

steps.title: New answer: טובת הנאה is just 'words'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason: the טובת הנאה of a כתובה is only 'words', and 'words' cannot be taken to pay a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the טובת הנאה is just words, and words are not mortgaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the רבי מאיר answer and gives a new one. She does not have to sell the טובת הנאה, because it is not something a debt can be collected from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טובת הנאה is not a real object. It is only a right that might pay out later. The גמרא suggests such a thin right does not count as property that is held for paying a debt, so the injured person cannot force her to sell it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the old answer for a new one)
Words, meaning a right on paper with no physical thing
Are held for (mortgaged to) paying a debt

phrases.english: Rather, the טובת הנאה is just words,
and words are not mortgaged (for a debt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 14 with a new answer to the question in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal reason replacing a rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טובת הנאה of a כתובה is a sellable asset she must use to pay the person she injured.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only 'words', and words are not held for paying debts.

steps.title: But these 'words' are sold for real money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'words' answer: this right is bought and sold for real money, so it should be usable to pay a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? They are words that are sold for dinars!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people pay real coins for the טובת הנאה, it has market value. Something with real value should be usable to pay a debt, so calling it 'just words' does not explain why she is exempt.

phrases.english: Why not?
They are words that are sold for dinars!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that טובת הנאה is 'words' that are not held for debts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It has real market value, since people buy it with money, so it should be usable to pay a debt.

steps.title: Third answer: שמואל's rule that a seller can cancel the debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with שמואל's rule: a person who sells a שטר חוב can still cancel the debt, and so can his heir. So selling her כתובה is unreliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of שמואל, for שמואל said: One who sells a שטר חוב to his friend and then cancels the debt, it is cancelled. And even an heir can cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reason she does not have to sell: שמואל's rule about cancelling a debt after selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, even after selling a debt, the original lender can still cancel it, and the buyer is left with nothing. In the same way, after she sells her כתובה rights she could cancel the כתובה to her husband. Because of this risk, she is not made to sell it.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule is a well-known principle: the right to collect a debt stays tied to the original lender, even after he sells the document.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of שמואל,
for שמואל said:
One who sells a שטר חוב to his friend,
and then went back and cancelled it, it is cancelled.
And even an heir can cancel it.
phrases.notes: He means the seller's heir also has this power to cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 16 with a new answer to the question in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside rule (שמואל) to explain the exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She could sell the טובת הנאה and pay the person she injured.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a seller can still cancel the debt, a sale of her כתובה is not reliable, so she is not made to sell it.

steps.title: Let her sell anyway, and if she cancels it, so be it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: let her sell and give the money to the injured person. If she later cancels the כתובה to her husband, let her cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Let her sell it and give him the money, and if she cancels it for the husband, let her cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the שמואל answer of step 17. The chance that she might cancel later should not stop her from selling now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every seller of a שטר חוב can cancel the debt, yet we still let people sell such documents. So her power to cancel should not exempt her. She should sell, pay the person she injured, and if she cancels later, that is the buyer's problem. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: They say: Let her sell it and give (the money) to him,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, making it 'let her sell'. 'Him' is the person she injured.

phrases.english: and if she cancels it for the husband,
let her cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the שמואל answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of שמואל's rule to exempt her from selling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The power to cancel later does not stop anyone else from selling a debt. So it should not stop her from selling now and paying the person she injured.

steps.title: She will surely forgive her husband, so we will not cause the buyer a loss
steps.stepSummary: A wife will certainly forgive her כתובה to her husband. בית דין will not have her sell it and so knowingly cause the buyer to lose his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: in anything that helps her husband, she will surely forgive the debt to him. (And we will not directly cause that buyer a loss.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push from step 18. Step 18 had said: let her sell, and if she later forgives the כתובה, so be it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 treated her forgiving the כתובה as only a possible risk. The answer says it is not just a risk. When it comes to her husband, she will surely forgive. So arranging such a sale would mean בית דין knowingly makes the buyer lose his money, and it will not do that.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (the usual way the גמרא brings an answer)
With regard to the husband; when it helps her husband

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up her husband with the buyer. She forgives the debt to the husband. The one who loses money is the buyer, who paid for a כתובה that has now been wiped out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the reason from 'forgiving is possible' to 'forgiving is certain.' That is why the sale is ruled out.

phrases.english: They say: in anything that concerns the husband,
phrases.notes: He means anything that would help her husband, like freeing him from paying the כתובה.

phrases.english: she will certainly forgive it to him.
(And causing a loss to that buyer
directly, we do not cause them a loss.)
phrases.notes: This sentence is in round brackets, so some versions of the גמרא have it and some leave it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כֹּל לְגַבֵּי בַעַל, וַדַּאי מָחֲלָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push in step 18 that she should simply sell and let her forgive the כתובה later if she wants.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual assumption: she will certainly forgive, so the sale knowingly causes a loss.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her forgiving the כתובה is only a possible risk, so the buyer can accept that risk.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her forgiving is certain when it helps her husband, so בית דין will not set up a sale that directly harms the buyer.

steps.title: Suggestion: let her sell it to the injured person himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new plan. She could sell her כתובה rights to the very person she injured, in exchange for its present value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let her sell it to the one she injured, for its present value,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new suggestion, and its answer comes next. Maybe she could sell her כתובה rights to the injured person himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in step 19 was hurting an outside buyer. If the buyer is the injured person, he is the one owed the money anyway. So the worry about causing a loss to an innocent buyer seems to go away.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a possible suggestion)
The present value of her right to collect the כתובה later

phrases.english: And if you would say: let her sell it to
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא; the corrected wording, in square brackets, means 'let her sell it.'

phrases.english: that one whom she injured
for its present value,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: תְּזַבְּנַיהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ לְהָהוּא דַּחֲבַלָה בֵּיהּ בְּטוֹבַת הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to get around step 19's concern about harming an outside buyer by making the injured person himself the buyer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of step 19 that her כתובה rights cannot be sold to pay the damages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the buyer is the injured person himself, there is no innocent outside buyer to protect. So the sale should be allowed.
